commits.author: rebel-jindol21
commits.message:
[Platform][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support (#4726)

* [feat][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support

Extend RblnDeviceOps to accept the MLA KV layout ([NB, BS, HS], single
latent plane) alongside the validated HND format. MLA layers get their
own functional gather/scatter op sequence (index_select + stack /
index_copy_) that stays on device-native v2v kernels and crosses the
device boundary with one DMA per chunk, since the shared torch path's
torch.empty staging falls back to CPU on RBLN.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [feat][RBLN] address MLA review comments and document the MLA layout

- Rename gather_blocks_to_chunk / scatter_chunk_to_blocks to *_hnd,
  matching the *_mla pair (review)
- Rename _SUPPORTED_FORMAT to _HND_FORMAT (review)
- Classify MLA via lmcache_native.is_mla() (review); unsupported MLA
  layouts are rejected at the format check with a format error instead
  of surfacing later as a shape mismatch in validate_mla_layers
- Document the MLA layout and its RBLN op sequence in the design README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [fix][RBLN] apply ruff-format to kv_ops.py

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [Platform][RBLN] Move MLA block transfer to device-staged _foreach_copy_

Review of #4726 asked for proof that the MLA op sequence (index_select +
stack, .to + index_copy_) does not take torch-rbln's CPU-fallback path on a
real vLLM-RBLN KV cache, and for a comparison against a block-view
_foreach_copy_ implementation.

Traced on DeepSeek-V3 (61 layers, dp8, VLLM_RBLN_USE_DEVICE_TENSOR=1,
torch-rbln 0.4.0rc0 / vllm-rbln 0.11.3a1): neither sequence hits any
torch-rbln bounce site or cpu_fallback, and store->retrieve is byte-exact
for both. The block-view design is adopted anyway:

- no index tensor, so no per-layer read-back of the index to the host
  (index_copy_ cannot take a CPU index, so a gather-side fix alone could
  not cover the scatter);
- every copy is a whole contiguous block, so it takes the direct memcpy_v2v
  path with no submit_or_fallback behind it;
- the L*B block copies of a chunk go through one batched d2d submission
  into a persistent per-thread device staging buffer and the chunk crosses
  the device boundary in one contiguous DMA. On par with the previous
  sequence at one block per chunk; 3.5-5x faster at 2-8 blocks per chunk
  (10-41 ms vs 37-213 ms per chunk on the real KV).

validate_mla_layers now also requires contiguous layers, since a permuted
view would silently send the block copies down the strided path. The
docstrings and README claiming the shared torch path falls to the CPU
fallback via a lazy torch.empty were not reproducible and are replaced by
the measured rationale. Adds a per-thread MLA staging test and a
contiguity test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

commits.message:
[MP][Ascend][KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples (#5138)

* [KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples

Detect and transfer per-layer plane tuples emitted by vLLM-Ascend for
DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA (latent, rope) and V3.2 DSA (latent, rope, dsa)
caches: every plane is a paged [NB, BS, 1, width] tensor with a single
latent KV head and mutually unequal widths. The transferred object stays
one flat plane of the summed width (kv_size == 1, is_mla); only the
paged source arrives as per-plane tuples.

- New EngineKVFormat value + format facts, pybind export, .pyi stub
- vLLM detector branch: single-head tuples of unequal widths (or arity
  1/3) classify as plane tuples; equal-width pairs stay (K, V)
- New spec NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS_Spec; NP stays symbolic like ONE/TWO
- Group per-layer format discovery by full shape/dtype structure
  (get_shape_and_dtype) so plane-tuple layers share one detection pass
- block-stride resolution accepts the format
- Python-fallback D2H/H2D transfer carving planes by byte offset,
  including mixed-item-size (int8 latent + fp16 scale) packing

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[MP][Coordinator] Add Kafka cache-event source (#5286)

Consume the fleet cache-event topic on the coordinator, so MP servers
that publish cache events to Kafka reach the key directory, usage view,
and eviction controller through the same gate as POST /events.

- KafkaCacheEventSource polls the topic on one thread and offers each
  record's CacheEventsRequest batches to EventGate.ingest_batches, so a
  partition (one instance's stream) is admitted in order. Offsets are
  stored only after the gate saw the record and committed by the
  consumer group: at-least-once, with the gate's dedup absorbing
  redelivery. Undecodable records and consumer exceptions are logged
  and skipped so one record cannot stall its partition.
- --event-transport {http,kafka} selects exactly one source (with
  --kafka-bootstrap-servers, --kafka-topic, --kafka-group-id under
  kafka); POST /events answers 404 under kafka. One path per emitter
  stream is what the gate's per-emitter seq cursor assumes.
- confluent-kafka ships as the optional lmcache[kafka] extra
  (requirements/kafka.txt) and is imported only when the source is
  built.
- Fake confluent_kafka consumer for deterministic tests, including an
  end-to-end create_app test that reads a record into the key directory
  and sees POST /events closed.
- Document the source in ingest.md, the design README, the coordinator
  guide, and the coordinator CLI reference.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: Daegyu Han
commits.message:
Reduce bringup time with parallel and batched recovery slot-header validation (#3835)

* raw_block: parallelize POSIX recovery header validation

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* raw_block: add recovery bringup benchmark

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

temp: refactor recovery validation layer separation

* raw_block: implement io_uring batched recovery header validation

Fill the regular io_uring multi-entry slot-header read path with
batched_read + wait_iouring over a pointer-aligned buffer.

Split the reads into iouring_queue_depth-sized batches so a large checkpoint
does not allocate one buffer for every entry at once, concatenating results
in input order. On a batched read error, fall back to per-slot reads within
that batch so a single bad slot is isolated instead of dropping every
recovered entry, matching the POSIX path.

NVMe passthrough (use_uring_cmd) recovery keeps the serial path; its
passthrough read needs separate validation before it can be batched.

Parameterize the recovery bringup benchmark by --io-engine (posix/io_uring)
so the POSIX thread-pool path and the io_uring batched-read path can be
compared on the same fixture.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* [Docs] Update raw-block recovery paths

Describe POSIX, regular io_uring, and uring_cmd recovery behavior.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* raw_block: enforce strict recovery header pairing

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* raw_block: retry only failed recovery headers

Check the io_uring completion bitmap so a failed slot header is reread
individually instead of dropping the recovered entry.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* Remove raw block recovery benchmark

Drop the raw-block-specific recovery benchmark from the general storage I/O
benchmark directory. Remove its README section so the documentation only
describes the remaining shared benchmark.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* Simplify chunked recovery header reads

Move the POSIX range reader into a private method and flatten the ordered
results from pool.map. Retain bounded range tasks to avoid creating one
future per slot during large checkpoint recovery.

Validation: all 47 raw-block core tests and file-scoped pre-commit checks
passed.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

commits.author: rebel-jindol21
commits.message:
[Platform][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support (#4726)

* [feat][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support

Extend RblnDeviceOps to accept the MLA KV layout ([NB, BS, HS], single
latent plane) alongside the validated HND format. MLA layers get their
own functional gather/scatter op sequence (index_select + stack /
index_copy_) that stays on device-native v2v kernels and crosses the
device boundary with one DMA per chunk, since the shared torch path's
torch.empty staging falls back to CPU on RBLN.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [feat][RBLN] address MLA review comments and document the MLA layout

- Rename gather_blocks_to_chunk / scatter_chunk_to_blocks to *_hnd,
  matching the *_mla pair (review)
- Rename _SUPPORTED_FORMAT to _HND_FORMAT (review)
- Classify MLA via lmcache_native.is_mla() (review); unsupported MLA
  layouts are rejected at the format check with a format error instead
  of surfacing later as a shape mismatch in validate_mla_layers
- Document the MLA layout and its RBLN op sequence in the design README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [fix][RBLN] apply ruff-format to kv_ops.py

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [Platform][RBLN] Move MLA block transfer to device-staged _foreach_copy_

Review of #4726 asked for proof that the MLA op sequence (index_select +
stack, .to + index_copy_) does not take torch-rbln's CPU-fallback path on a
real vLLM-RBLN KV cache, and for a comparison against a block-view
_foreach_copy_ implementation.

Traced on DeepSeek-V3 (61 layers, dp8, VLLM_RBLN_USE_DEVICE_TENSOR=1,
torch-rbln 0.4.0rc0 / vllm-rbln 0.11.3a1): neither sequence hits any
torch-rbln bounce site or cpu_fallback, and store->retrieve is byte-exact
for both. The block-view design is adopted anyway:

- no index tensor, so no per-layer read-back of the index to the host
  (index_copy_ cannot take a CPU index, so a gather-side fix alone could
  not cover the scatter);
- every copy is a whole contiguous block, so it takes the direct memcpy_v2v
  path with no submit_or_fallback behind it;
- the L*B block copies of a chunk go through one batched d2d submission
  into a persistent per-thread device staging buffer and the chunk crosses
  the device boundary in one contiguous DMA. On par with the previous
  sequence at one block per chunk; 3.5-5x faster at 2-8 blocks per chunk
  (10-41 ms vs 37-213 ms per chunk on the real KV).

validate_mla_layers now also requires contiguous layers, since a permuted
view would silently send the block copies down the strided path. The
docstrings and README claiming the shared torch path falls to the CPU
fallback via a lazy torch.empty were not reproducible and are replaced by
the measured rationale. Adds a per-thread MLA staging test and a
contiguity test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

commits.author: Daegyu Han
commits.message:
Reduce bringup time with parallel and batched recovery slot-header validation (#3835)

* raw_block: parallelize POSIX recovery header validation

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* raw_block: add recovery bringup benchmark

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

temp: refactor recovery validation layer separation

* raw_block: implement io_uring batched recovery header validation

Fill the regular io_uring multi-entry slot-header read path with
batched_read + wait_iouring over a pointer-aligned buffer.

Split the reads into iouring_queue_depth-sized batches so a large checkpoint
does not allocate one buffer for every entry at once, concatenating results
in input order. On a batched read error, fall back to per-slot reads within
that batch so a single bad slot is isolated instead of dropping every
recovered entry, matching the POSIX path.

NVMe passthrough (use_uring_cmd) recovery keeps the serial path; its
passthrough read needs separate validation before it can be batched.

Parameterize the recovery bringup benchmark by --io-engine (posix/io_uring)
so the POSIX thread-pool path and the io_uring batched-read path can be
compared on the same fixture.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* [Docs] Update raw-block recovery paths

Describe POSIX, regular io_uring, and uring_cmd recovery behavior.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* raw_block: enforce strict recovery header pairing

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* raw_block: retry only failed recovery headers

Check the io_uring completion bitmap so a failed slot header is reread
individually instead of dropping the recovered entry.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* Remove raw block recovery benchmark

Drop the raw-block-specific recovery benchmark from the general storage I/O
benchmark directory. Remove its README section so the documentation only
describes the remaining shared benchmark.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* Simplify chunked recovery header reads

Move the POSIX range reader into a private method and flatten the ordered
results from pool.map. Retain bounded range tasks to avoid creating one
future per slot during large checkpoint recovery.

Validation: all 47 raw-block core tests and file-scoped pre-commit checks
passed.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

commits.author: Junyuan
commits.message:
[MP][Ascend][KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples (#5138)

* [KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples

Detect and transfer per-layer plane tuples emitted by vLLM-Ascend for
DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA (latent, rope) and V3.2 DSA (latent, rope, dsa)
caches: every plane is a paged [NB, BS, 1, width] tensor with a single
latent KV head and mutually unequal widths. The transferred object stays
one flat plane of the summed width (kv_size == 1, is_mla); only the
paged source arrives as per-plane tuples.

- New EngineKVFormat value + format facts, pybind export, .pyi stub
- vLLM detector branch: single-head tuples of unequal widths (or arity
  1/3) classify as plane tuples; equal-width pairs stay (K, V)
- New spec NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS_Spec; NP stays symbolic like ONE/TWO
- Group per-layer format discovery by full shape/dtype structure
  (get_shape_and_dtype) so plane-tuple layers share one detection pass
- block-stride resolution accepts the format
- Python-fallback D2H/H2D transfer carving planes by byte offset,
  including mixed-item-size (int8 latent + fp16 scale) packing

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[MP][Coordinator] Add Kafka cache-event source (#5286)

Consume the fleet cache-event topic on the coordinator, so MP servers
that publish cache events to Kafka reach the key directory, usage view,
and eviction controller through the same gate as POST /events.

- KafkaCacheEventSource polls the topic on one thread and offers each
  record's CacheEventsRequest batches to EventGate.ingest_batches, so a
  partition (one instance's stream) is admitted in order. Offsets are
  stored only after the gate saw the record and committed by the
  consumer group: at-least-once, with the gate's dedup absorbing
  redelivery. Undecodable records and consumer exceptions are logged
  and skipped so one record cannot stall its partition.
- --event-transport {http,kafka} selects exactly one source (with
  --kafka-bootstrap-servers, --kafka-topic, --kafka-group-id under
  kafka); POST /events answers 404 under kafka. One path per emitter
  stream is what the gate's per-emitter seq cursor assumes.
- confluent-kafka ships as the optional lmcache[kafka] extra
  (requirements/kafka.txt) and is imported only when the source is
  built.
- Fake confluent_kafka consumer for deterministic tests, including an
  end-to-end create_app test that reads a record into the key directory
  and sees POST /events closed.
- Document the source in ingest.md, the design README, the coordinator
  guide, and the coordinator CLI reference.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: rebel-jindol21
commits.message:
[Platform][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support (#4726)

* [feat][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support

Extend RblnDeviceOps to accept the MLA KV layout ([NB, BS, HS], single
latent plane) alongside the validated HND format. MLA layers get their
own functional gather/scatter op sequence (index_select + stack /
index_copy_) that stays on device-native v2v kernels and crosses the
device boundary with one DMA per chunk, since the shared torch path's
torch.empty staging falls back to CPU on RBLN.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [feat][RBLN] address MLA review comments and document the MLA layout

- Rename gather_blocks_to_chunk / scatter_chunk_to_blocks to *_hnd,
  matching the *_mla pair (review)
- Rename _SUPPORTED_FORMAT to _HND_FORMAT (review)
- Classify MLA via lmcache_native.is_mla() (review); unsupported MLA
  layouts are rejected at the format check with a format error instead
  of surfacing later as a shape mismatch in validate_mla_layers
- Document the MLA layout and its RBLN op sequence in the design README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [fix][RBLN] apply ruff-format to kv_ops.py

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

* [Platform][RBLN] Move MLA block transfer to device-staged _foreach_copy_

Review of #4726 asked for proof that the MLA op sequence (index_select +
stack, .to + index_copy_) does not take torch-rbln's CPU-fallback path on a
real vLLM-RBLN KV cache, and for a comparison against a block-view
_foreach_copy_ implementation.

Traced on DeepSeek-V3 (61 layers, dp8, VLLM_RBLN_USE_DEVICE_TENSOR=1,
torch-rbln 0.4.0rc0 / vllm-rbln 0.11.3a1): neither sequence hits any
torch-rbln bounce site or cpu_fallback, and store->retrieve is byte-exact
for both. The block-view design is adopted anyway:

- no index tensor, so no per-layer read-back of the index to the host
  (index_copy_ cannot take a CPU index, so a gather-side fix alone could
  not cover the scatter);
- every copy is a whole contiguous block, so it takes the direct memcpy_v2v
  path with no submit_or_fallback behind it;
- the L*B block copies of a chunk go through one batched d2d submission
  into a persistent per-thread device staging buffer and the chunk crosses
  the device boundary in one contiguous DMA. On par with the previous
  sequence at one block per chunk; 3.5-5x faster at 2-8 blocks per chunk
  (10-41 ms vs 37-213 ms per chunk on the real KV).

validate_mla_layers now also requires contiguous layers, since a permuted
view would silently send the block copies down the strided path. The
docstrings and README claiming the shared torch path falls to the CPU
fallback via a lazy torch.empty were not reproducible and are replaced by
the measured rationale. Adds a per-thread MLA staging test and a
contiguity test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jindol21 <jindol21@rebellions.ai>

commits.author: Daegyu Han
commits.message:
Reduce bringup time with parallel and batched recovery slot-header validation (#3835)

* raw_block: parallelize POSIX recovery header validation

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* raw_block: add recovery bringup benchmark

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

temp: refactor recovery validation layer separation

* raw_block: implement io_uring batched recovery header validation

Fill the regular io_uring multi-entry slot-header read path with
batched_read + wait_iouring over a pointer-aligned buffer.

Split the reads into iouring_queue_depth-sized batches so a large checkpoint
does not allocate one buffer for every entry at once, concatenating results
in input order. On a batched read error, fall back to per-slot reads within
that batch so a single bad slot is isolated instead of dropping every
recovered entry, matching the POSIX path.

NVMe passthrough (use_uring_cmd) recovery keeps the serial path; its
passthrough read needs separate validation before it can be batched.

Parameterize the recovery bringup benchmark by --io-engine (posix/io_uring)
so the POSIX thread-pool path and the io_uring batched-read path can be
compared on the same fixture.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* [Docs] Update raw-block recovery paths

Describe POSIX, regular io_uring, and uring_cmd recovery behavior.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* raw_block: enforce strict recovery header pairing

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* raw_block: retry only failed recovery headers

Check the io_uring completion bitmap so a failed slot header is reread
individually instead of dropping the recovered entry.

Signed-off-by: Nayeon Kim <nayeoni.kim@samsung.com>

* Remove raw block recovery benchmark

Drop the raw-block-specific recovery benchmark from the general storage I/O
benchmark directory. Remove its README section so the documentation only
describes the remaining shared benchmark.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

* Simplify chunked recovery header reads

Move the POSIX range reader into a private method and flatten the ordered
results from pool.map. Retain bounded range tasks to avoid creating one
future per slot during large checkpoint recovery.

Validation: all 47 raw-block core tests and file-scoped pre-commit checks
passed.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <daegyu94.han@samsung.com>

commits.author: Junyuan
commits.message:
[MP][Ascend][KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples (#5138)

* [KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples

Detect and transfer per-layer plane tuples emitted by vLLM-Ascend for
DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA (latent, rope) and V3.2 DSA (latent, rope, dsa)
caches: every plane is a paged [NB, BS, 1, width] tensor with a single
latent KV head and mutually unequal widths. The transferred object stays
one flat plane of the summed width (kv_size == 1, is_mla); only the
paged source arrives as per-plane tuples.

- New EngineKVFormat value + format facts, pybind export, .pyi stub
- vLLM detector branch: single-head tuples of unequal widths (or arity
  1/3) classify as plane tuples; equal-width pairs stay (K, V)
- New spec NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS_Spec; NP stays symbolic like ONE/TWO
- Group per-layer format discovery by full shape/dtype structure
  (get_shape_and_dtype) so plane-tuple layers share one detection pass
- block-stride resolution accepts the format
- Python-fallback D2H/H2D transfer carving planes by byte offset,
  including mixed-item-size (int8 latent + fp16 scale) packing
